patients.label: 72-year-old woman with exertional breathlessness, Swyer-James-MacLeod syndrome in the left lung and pulmonary fibrosis in the right lung

identity_evidence.quote: A 72-year-old Caucasian female patient was referred to the respiratory clinic

attribution_limitations: The CT text says the right-lung findings suggest an underlying pulmonary fibrosis, while the abstract, discussion and learning points state idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis as the diagnosis. No biopsy, multidisciplinary discussion or clinical-radiological criteria for IPF are reported, so the condition is recorded as provisional.
The paragraph reports a 6-month history of exertional breathlessness yet also states that exercise tolerance was unlimited and she enjoyed good health.
The paragraph says she was on prednisolone 1 mg for polymyalgia rheumatica but "not on any regular medications" otherwise; whether prednisolone was still being taken at presentation is not stated.
The authors say the 2-year-prior radiograph suggested left-lung radiolucency; the relation of "2 years later" radiographs to the presentation date is only stated relative to the initial radiograph.

The authors state eosinophilic pneumonia was not suspected despite a high lavage eosinophil count, and that it is difficult to tell whether the affected left lung is larger, normal or smaller than the contralateral fibrotic lung; neither is a measured result.
The discussion proposes that SJMS is "protective" against IPF in the affected lung; this is an authors' hypothesis, not a patient finding.

PET CT showed reduced FDG uptake in the left lung.
